Riding light (first light to last light, Vancouver): Sun, Nov 15 7:48am to 6:06pm; Mon, Nov 16 7:49am to 6:05pm; Tue, Nov 17 7:51am to 6:04pm. Hours outside that are dark and not listed; never suggest riding then.

Guillermo's own take for Sun, Nov 15 (his read, quote it as his, not yours): The southerly is in Howe Sound. Pam Rocks is S 23 gusting 30 at 6am and building, and the Spit has settled to 14 to 17 after a 19 to 26 burst at dawn, right on the page.

Porteau may work if Pam Rocks holds but the flood to 14.8ft near 11:30 can kill the swell.  Ferry Terminal is blowing now and may last for a few hours.

EC marine forecast, Howe Sound (issued 10:30 AM PCT 15 November 2026), WARNING IN EFFECT: Today Tonight and Monday. Wind southerly inflow 10 to 20 knots becoming southerly inflow 5 to 15 early this evening except southeasterly inflow 20 over southern sections tonight. Wind becoming northerly outflow 5 to 15 Monday afternoon. Strong wind warning program has ended for the season.

EC marine forecast, Strait of Georgia (south of Nanaimo) (issued 10:30 AM PCT 15 November 2026): Today Tonight and Monday. Wind southeast 15 to 20 knots veering to south 5 to 15 this afternoon then backing to southeast 15 to 20 this evening. Wind diminishing to southeast 5 to 15 near noon Monday then becoming light Monday evening. Strong wind warning program has ended for the season.
